messages:
oncall-bot: Pager ⚠️ KV-cache growth observed for model redwood-phi-7b (us-west-2). Rapid memory growth on kv-store shard-12, continuous-batcher queue length > 800, p95 token latency up 3.8x. AlertID ALERT-9876
joel: acked. I'll jump in — collecting traces and current batch config.
sara: seeing a lot of small prefixes being miss-hits causing new cache entries. metric: kv.entries/s spike from 3k -> 110k in 30m. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dash/kv/growth
vishal: recent deploy at 04:12 changed continuous_batch.max_window from 256 -> 1024, suspect batching policy expansion causing cache amplification and longer-lived KV keys.
kate: also saw tokenizer drift for a subset of prompts — template expansion added a hidden unicode char which changes prompt-hash. That would create many unique keys.
joel: good call. can we confirm template drift? any diffs in the templating service? @dana can you pull last 100 template commits?
dana: pulling now. quick grep shows commit e7b3f12 added `\u200b` in rendering for legacy templates. suspect that explains new unique prefixes.
joel: ok plan: 1) throttle batching to reduce continuous_batch.max_window to 128 via hotpatch 2) invalidate prefix cache for affected model shards 3) restart a subset of inference workers on shard-12 to reclaim memory 4) follow-up: backfill template fix and rotate prompt-hash keys if needed.
vishal: agree. I'll cut the hotpatch. patch command:
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/patch -d '{"target":"continuous_batch","model":"redwood-phi-7b","max_window":128}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN'
```
joel: applying now.
oncall-bot: deploy-bot: Starting hotpatch job job-4321. ETA ~ 60s.
incidents-bot: Incident CREATED | sev: high | lead: joel | impact: increased latency for generation endpoints; potential customer rate-limiting.
joel: hotpatch applied to us-west-2 pool. Observing queue length dropping to ~200. p95 latency trending down.
sara: started prefix-cache invalidation for model redwood-phi-7b shards [10..14] with safe-rate 50/s. command used: `servicectl cache invalidate --model redwood-phi-7b --prefix-regex "^tmpl/legacy/" --rate 50`
kate: meanwhile pushed small rendering fix to templating-service (remove stray \u200b). PR: https://git.redwood/p/tmpl/123. Will roll forward canary after cache stabilizes.
dana: template fix merged and deployed to canary (tmpl-canary-2). No regressions seen in sampling.
luis: incoming handoff — I'll take second shift. summary for oncall: hotpatch throttled batching, invalidated legacy prefixes, restarted 4 workers on shard-12. Current state: kv.entries still elevated but dropping, p95 ~= 1.2x baseline, no errors in customer responses.
joel: handing off to @luis. notes: watch kv.entries and batch-queue-length, be ready to roll model to a lower-capacity variant if memory doesn't return. escalation: +1 to infra if kv bucket exceeds 1.5M entries.
luis: ack — taking over. setting heartbeat every 30m.
incidents-bot: Update: mitigation in progress. severity review scheduled in 30m.
dana: quick check on customers: estimated impacted orgs = 12 (mostly sandbox customers); top 3 saw 30-80% latency increase; no errors or data corruption. I opened support ticket batch for affected customers (SUP-4456).
vishal: postmortem action items (rough): 1) disallow invisible unicode in templates via linter 2) add prefix-hash versioning to tolerate template rendering changes 3) add automatic batch-throttle when kv growth rate exceeds threshold 4) improve observability so we can correlate template commits -> kv growth in 5m windows.
sara: additional mitigation: set a temporary global cache cap for prefix cache at 2M keys to force eviction. doing that now: `kvctl set-cap --model redwood-phi-7b --cap 2000000`
luis: confirm eviction triggered, free memory reclaimed on shard-12. kv.entries now ~420k, p95 stable at 1.1x baseline.
joel: nice work team. I'll draft incident summary and timeline. tag me on the postmortem PR. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: Incident UPDATED | status: mitigated | mitigations: batching hotpatch, template fix, prefix invalidation, worker restarts | duration: ~2.2h
luis: handing off to regular oncall tomorrow morning. closing live coordination. next: postmortem and customer comms in #support.
joel: final note — customers impacted were sandbox/test accounts; prod customers not affected beyond small latency blips. closing thread but leaving logs and commands in the incident doc.
